+---
+layout: docs
+page_title: Configure Microsoft Entra ID for agent IAM
+description: >-
+   Use Microsoft Entra ID and Vault to secure agent permissions with App registrations, OAuth resource server profiles, and entity aliases.
+---
+
+# Configure Microsoft Entra ID for agent IAM
+
+@include 'alerts/beta.mdx'
+
+@include 'alerts/enterprise-and-hcp.mdx'
+
+Configure an App registration and OAuth resource server profile in Microsoft Entra ID to use with Vault Enterprise agentic IAM.
+
+## Before you start
+
+- **You must have admin access** to an Azure Tenant/Subscription.
+
+- **You must have enough permissions** to create an App registration.
+
+- **You must have [`curl`](https://curl.se/)** or some other tool to make API calls.
+
+- **You must have [`jq`](https://jqlang.org/) installed** to use the example commands as written.
+
+## Step 1: Create an App registration
+
+Create a new **App Registration** that represents your agent's authentication entry point.
+
+1. Select **App registrations**.
+
+   ![App registrations banner](/img/agentic-ai/screenshot-entra-app-registrations.png)
+
+1. Select **New Registration**.
+
+   ![new registration list](/img/agentic-ai/screenshot-entra-new-registration.png)
+
+1. Name the App registration `vault-oauth-test`. The default values are fine for everything else. Then choose **Register** at the bottom.
+
+   ![Update the name for the App registration](/img/agentic-ai/screenshot-entra-name-it.png)
+
+## Step 2: Create a client secret
+
+Create a client secret under the App registration. Your agent uses this secret to authenticate with Microsoft Entra ID.
+
+1. Select the **Certificates & secrets** in the **Manage** section.
+
+1. Select **+ New client secret**.
+
+1. Enter a description and set an appropriate expiration.
+
+   ![Add a new client secret](/img/agentic-ai/screenshot-entra-new-client-secret.png)
+
+   Click **Add** at the bottom.
+
+1. Copy the secret name, value and ID.  You will use these values in a later step.
+
+## Step 3: Expose an API for App registration
+
+Generate an Application ID URI by exposing an API for the App registration. For  scoped token requests, Application ID URI identifies the resource server.
+
+1. Select **Expose an API** in the left navigation panel.
+
+1. Click **Add** next to **Application ID URI**. The default is fine for now, and choose **Save** at the bottom.
+
+1. Copy the **Application ID URI** for use later.  You will use these values in a later step.
+
+## Step 4: Update App registration manifest
+
+Add `requestedAccessTokenVersion: 2` to the manifest so Entra ID issues an access token that Vault can validate.  You will use these values in a later step.
+
+1. Click **Manifest** and add `”requestedAccessTokenVersion”: 2` to the manifest in the `api` section.
+
+   <CodeBlockConfig hideClipboard>
+
+   ```json
+      ...
+      "api": {
+         "acceptMappedClaims": null,
+         "knownClientApplications": [],
+         "requestedAccessTokenVersion": 2,
+         "oauth2PermissionScopes": [],
+         "preAuthorizedApplications": []
+      },
+      ... 
+   ```
+
+   </CodeBlockConfig>
+
+   Click **Save**.
+
+## Step 5: Gather OAuth metadata
+
+Vault needs some information to configure the OAuth resource server config Profile. For this example setup you need to find the `issuer_id`, `jwks_uri`, and `token_endpoint`.
+
+1. Select **Overview** in the left navigation panel.
+
+1. Select **Endpoints**.
+
+1. Find the **OpenID Connect metadata document URL** and copy it.
+
+1. Using the **OpenID Connect metadata document URL** run the following `curl` command to fetch the metadata document.
+
+   ```shell-session
+   $ curl -s <YOUR OPEN ID METADATA DOCUMENT URL> | jq -r "{token_endpoint, jwks_uri, issuer}"
+   ```
+
+   The response is a JSON document. Note the `token_endpoint`, `jwks_uri`, and `issuer` values for use later.
+
+   **Example output:**
+   
+   <CodeBlockConfig hideClipboard>
+   
+   ```json
+   {
+      "token_endpoint": "https://login.microsoftonline.com/0e3e2e88-8caf-41ca-b4da-e3b33b6c52ec/oauth2/v2.0/token",
+      "jwks_uri": "https://login.microsoftonline.com/0e3e2e88-8caf-41ca-b4da-e3b33b6c52ec/discovery/v2.0/keys",
+      "issuer": "https://login.microsoftonline.com/0e3e2e88-8caf-41ca-b4da-e3b33b6c52ec/v2.0",
+   }
+   ```
+  
+   </CodeBlockConfig>
+
+1. Close out the **Endpoints** page. You are back on the **Overview**.
+
+1. Select your application name next to **Managed application in local directory**.
+
+   ![Name of the managed application in local directory](/img/agentic-ai/screenshot-entra-managed-application.png)
+
+1. Copy the **Object ID** and save for later.  You will use these values in a later step.
+
+   ![Find the Object ID](/img/agentic-ai/screenshot-entra-object-id.png)
+
+1. Using these gathered values export environment variables using the values from the OpenID Connect metadata document.  Copy and update these with the following table.
+
+   | Noted value | environmental variable | Explanation |
+   |------|------|------|
+   | Object ID | EXTERNAL_ID | a globally unique identifier (GUID) for the application |
+   | Token endpoint | TOKEN_ENDPOINT | Endpoint used to obtain access and ID tokens|
+   | JSON Web Key Set URI | JWKS_URI | Endpoint that provides public cryptographic keys in JSON format |
+   | Issuer URL | ISSUER | URL identifying  identity provider |
+
+   Export these values as environment variables for use in Vault commands.
+
+   ```shell-session
+   export                                    \
+      VAULT_ADDR="http://127.0.0.1:8200"     \
+      VAULT_TOKEN="root"                     \
+      EXTERNAL_ID=<YOUR OBJECT ID>         \
+      TOKEN_ENDPOINT=<YOUR TOKEN ENDPOINT>   \
+      JWKS_URI=<YOUR JWKS URI>               \
+      ISSUER=<YOUR ISSUER URI>               \
+      APP_ID=<YOUR APP ID>                   \
+      SECRET_VALUE=<YOUR SECRET VALUE>
+   ```
+
+## Step 6: Configure Vault for Entra ID
+
+Use the values gathered from Microsoft Entra ID to configure an OAuth resource server profile in Vault that validates agent JWTs.
+
+<Note>
+
+   Microsoft Entra ID JWTs use `uti` as the unique identifier claim instead of the standard `jti`. Set `unique_id_claim` to `uti` and set `optional_authorization_details` to `false` to make the `authorization_details` claim optional in issued JWTs.

+---
+layout: "vault"
+page_title: "Vault: vault_tpm_auth_backend_role resource"
+sidebar_current: "docs-vault-resource-vault-tpm-auth-backend-role"
+description: |-
+  Manages TPM auth backend roles in Vault.
+---
+
+# vault\_tpm\_auth\_backend\_role
+
+Manages a role in a TPM (Trusted Platform Module) auth backend. Roles define the mapping
+from TPM identities and TPM groups to Vault policies and token parameters.
+
+~> **Important** This resource requires Vault 2.2.0 or later.
+
+## Example Usage
+
+```hcl
+resource "vault_auth_backend" "tpm" {
+  type = "tpm"
+  path = "tpm"
+}
+
+resource "vault_tpm_auth_backend_role" "example" {
+  mount        = vault_auth_backend.tpm.path
+  name         = "example-role"
+  display_name = "Example TPM Role"
+  cert_ttl     = "720h"
+  
+  tpm_ids = [
+    "abc123...",
+    "def456..."
+  ]
+  
+  tpmgroup_ids = [
+    "group-1",
+    "group-2"
+  ]
+  
+  token_ttl         = 3600
+  token_max_ttl     = 7200
+  token_policies    = ["default", "tpm-policy"]
+  token_bound_cidrs = ["10.0.0.0/8"]
+}
+```
+
+## Argument Reference
+
+The following arguments are supported:
+
+* `namespace` - (Optional) The namespace to provision the resource in.
+  The value should not contain leading or trailing forward slashes.
+  The `namespace` is always relative to the provider's configured [namespace](/docs/providers/vault/index.html#namespace).
+   *Available only for Vault Enterprise*.
+
+* `mount` - (Required) TPM auth backend mount path.
+
+* `name` - (Required) Name of the TPM role.
+
+* `display_name` - (Optional) Display name for the role. Defaults to the role name.
+
+* `cert_ttl` - (Optional) Certificate TTL for the TPM role. Accepts duration format strings
+  (e.g., "720h", "30d"). If not specified, uses the backend's default.
+
+* `tpm_ids` - (Optional) Set of TPM record IDs authorized to authenticate with this role.
+  These are the unique IDs assigned by Vault to TPM records (SHA256 of the EK public key).
+
+* `tpmgroup_ids` - (Optional) Set of TPM group IDs authorized to authenticate with this role.
+
+### Common Token Arguments

issue.title: aws_cloudfront_distribution_tenant: Fix inconsistent result after apply error when creating an aws_cloudfront_distribution_tenant with a managed_certificate_request block and no explicit customizations block

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Addresses a defect in current functionality.

labels.name: size/XL
labels.description: Managed by automation to categorize the size of a PR.

labels.name: tests
labels.description: PRs: expanded test coverage. Issues: expanded coverage, enhancements to test infrastructure.

labels.name: service/cloudfront
labels.description: Issues and PRs that pertain to the cloudfront service.

issue.body:
## Description

  Fixes the Provider produced inconsistent result after apply error when creating an aws_cloudfront_distribution_tenant with a managed_certificate_request block and no explicit customizations block.

 ## Root cause

  When managed_certificate_request is used, CloudFront issues a managed certificate and auto-populates customizations.certificate in the API response — even though the practitioner never configured a customizations block. The provider flattened that response straight
  into state, so:

  - plan had customizations block count 0 (nothing in config), but
  - state had block count 1 (the service-injected certificate).

  Terraform core rejects this mismatch (.customizations[0].certificate: block count changed from 0 to 1). The resource is tainted, and the next plan schedules a destroy + recreate of a working tenant — at scale (e.g. CloudFront-for-SaaS migrations) this is
  operationally untenable and can cause customer-facing TLS gaps.

 ##  Fix

  In Create, Read, and Update, reconcile the API-injected certificate against the practitioner's configuration via a helper (suppressManagedCertCustomizations) that runs only when a managed certificate is in play and the user did not explicitly configure a
  certificate sub-block. It operates at the certificate sub-block level (not the whole customizations block), so it covers both:

  1. No customizations block at all — the reported case; planned value (null) is preserved.
  2. customizations with web_acl/geo_restriction but no certificate — only the injected certificate sub-block is suppressed; the practitioner's other sub-blocks and any server-computed values are preserved.

  An explicitly configured customizations.certificate is always passed through unchanged. In Read, the reconciliation is gated on the prior managed_certificate_request so that terraform import (which passes through only the id) round-trips an explicitly configured
  certificate correctly.

  This makes plan == apply, eliminating both the create-time error and the spurious destroy + recreate. No HCL changes are required and the change is non-breaking.

 ## Testing

  - Unit test — TestSuppressManagedCertCustomizations exercises every branch of the reconciliation helper (planned null, planned unknown, planned empty, explicit certificate pass-through, geo_restriction without certificate, and the combined geo_restriction +
  injected-certificate case). ✅ PASS
  - Acceptance test — TestAccCloudFrontDistributionTenant_managedCertificateRequest (create with managed_certificate_request, assert empty follow-up plan). ✅ PASS
  - go vet passes; gofmt clean.

thank ya @gerrytan abuot the SDKv2 it does skips

i did try the union (Member/Owner | UUID | numeric), but the Graph docs pushed me off it 
originId is whatever the origin system says it is (for SharePoint it's "the sequence number of the role in the site"), and originSystem is documented as "such as SharePointOnline, AadApplication, AzureResources or AadGroup".

- beta: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/api/resources/accesspackageresourcerole?view=graph-rest-beta
- v1.0: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/api/resources/accesspackageresourcerole?view=graph-rest-1.0

also realized the union would block AzureResources at plan time, which is the same over-tight validation behind #1066/#1637/#1776 the other prs i think

the docs does mention roles can be expanded from the catalog resource, and create already lists that resource so access_type is now matched against the roles the service actually reports, by origin ID or display name, and an unknown value errors with the roles that are available. 

that is why i left the schema validation as `StringIsNotEmpty`: the real check now happens where the origin system is actually known 

i did test on my live tenant and was able to pass all the test successfully

oh also ran into a small bug tho when testing so the roles aren't reported immediately after a resource is onboarded (which we know graph can be bit slow at times), so an association created in the same apply could and did fail with `RoleNotFound`. A re-apply did bring it back to the right state, but create now waits for the roles instead so that might be a better long-term fix ?

issue.title: google_container_cluster: switching maintenance_policy window type (daily ↔ recurring) never clears the previous window, causing a perpetual diff

labels.name: forward/review
labels.description: In review; remove label to forward

issue.body:
### Community Note

* Please vote on this issue by adding a 👍 [reaction](https://blog.github.com/2016-03-10-add-reactions-to-pull-requests-issues-and-comments/) to the original issue to help the community and maintainers prioritize this request.
* Please do not leave _+1_ or _me too_ comments, they generate extra noise for issue followers and do not help prioritize the request.
* If you are interested in working on this issue or have submitted a pull request, please leave a comment.
* If an issue is assigned to a user, that user is claiming responsibility for the issue.

### Terraform Version & Provider Version(s)

Reproduced against current `master` of `resource_container_cluster.go` (shared source between `google` and `google-beta` via magic-modules); not tied to a specific released version.

### Affected Resource(s)

* `google_container_cluster`

### Terraform Configuration

Before:
```tf
resource "google_container_cluster" "example" {
  # ... other config

  maintenance_policy {
    daily_maintenance_window {
      start_time = "06:00"
    }
  }
}
```

After:
```tf
resource "google_container_cluster" "example" {
  # ... other config

  maintenance_policy {
    recurring_window {
      start_time = "2026-09-03T06:00:00Z"
      end_time   = "2026-09-03T10:00:00Z"
      recurrence = "FREQ=DAILY"
    }
  }
}
```

### Debug Output

Not applicable — this isn't a crash or an error, it's a silent no-op. See "Actual Behavior" for the observable symptom (a diff that never resolves).

### Expected Behavior

After `terraform apply`, the cluster's maintenance policy is `recurring_window` only, `daily_maintenance_window` is cleared, and the next `plan` is clean.

### Actual Behavior

`apply` succeeds and the provider's own state shows `recurring_window`, but the live GCP resource never actually drops `daily_maintenance_window` — confirmed with `gcloud container clusters describe <cluster> --format="yaml(maintenancePolicy)"`, which keeps returning:

```yaml
maintenancePolicy:
  window:
    dailyMaintenanceWindow:
      duration: PT4H0M0S
      startTime: '06:00'
    # recurringWindow never actually appears here
```

Because the real resource never matches config, every subsequent `plan`/`apply` detects the identical diff again and reapplies — forever, with no error surfaced anywhere.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Create a `google_container_cluster` with `maintenance_policy.daily_maintenance_window` set.
2. `terraform apply`.
3. Change the config to `maintenance_policy.recurring_window` instead (remove the `daily_maintenance_window` block).
4. `terraform apply` again — it reports success.
5. Run `terraform plan` — it shows the same `recurring_window` diff again, unchanged.
6. Independently check `gcloud container clusters describe <cluster> --format="yaml(maintenancePolicy)"` — `dailyMaintenanceWindow` is still present, `recurringWindow` never appears.

### Important Factoids

Root cause, traced in provider source (not inferred from behavior alone):

1. `resourceContainerClusterUpdate` calls the dedicated `Projects.Locations.Clusters.SetMaintenancePolicy` RPC on `d.HasChange("maintenance_policy")` (`resource_container_cluster.go:4991-5010`) — a whole-object-replace call, not a masked patch, so the API should apply the `window` oneof correctly given a request that omits the old branch.

2. `expandMaintenancePolicy()` (`resource_container_cluster.go:6324-6437`), when `recurring_window` is configured, builds:
   ```go
   &container.MaintenancePolicy{
       Window: &container.MaintenanceWindow{
           MaintenanceExclusions: exclusions,
           RecurringWindow: &container.RecurringTimeWindow{...},
       },
       ...
   }
   ```
   `DailyMaintenanceWindow` is left at its Go zero value (`nil`). Nothing sets `NullFields`/`ForceSendFields` for the sibling window type being vacated — the same gap exists in the `daily_maintenance_window` and `recurring_maintenance_window` branches.

3. In the generated `google-api-go-client` struct (`container/v1/container-gen.go`, `MaintenanceWindow`):
   ```go
   DailyMaintenanceWindow *DailyMaintenanceWindow `json:"dailyMaintenanceWindow,omitempty"`
   ...
   ForceSendFields []string `json:"-"`
   NullFields      []string `json:"-"`
   ```
   A `nil` pointer tagged `omitempty` is dropped from the JSON body entirely unless named in `NullFields`. Since `expandMaintenancePolicy()` never populates it, the outbound request simply never mentions `dailyMaintenanceWindow` — it isn't cleared, it's just absent, and GKE leaves the existing value untouched.

**Suggested fix**: in `expandMaintenancePolicy()`, when building the `MaintenanceWindow` for whichever type is configured, explicitly set `NullFields` for the sibling types being vacated, e.g. for `recurring_window`:

```go
window := &container.MaintenanceWindow{
    MaintenanceExclusions: exclusions,
    RecurringWindow: &container.RecurringTimeWindow{...},
}
window.NullFields = append(window.NullFields, "DailyMaintenanceWindow", "RecurringMaintenanceWindow")
```

(symmetrically for the other two branches).

**Workaround**: run `gcloud container clusters update <cluster> --maintenance-window-start=... --maintenance-window-end=... --maintenance-window-recurrence=...` (or the daily-window equivalent) once, outside Terraform. That client path clears the sibling field correctly, so the real resource matches and the next `plan` comes back clean.

### References

* `google-api-go-client`: `container/v1/container-gen.go`, `MaintenanceWindow` struct and its `MarshalJSON`/`NullFields` mechanism.

   ```go
   ForceSendFields []string `json:"-"`
   NullFields      []string `json:"-"`
   ```
   A `nil` pointer tagged `omitempty` is dropped from the JSON body entirely unless named in `NullFields`. Since `expandMaintenancePolicy()` never populates it, the outbound request simply never mentions `dailyMaintenanceWindow` — it isn't cleared, it's just absent, and GKE leaves the existing value untouched.

**Suggested fix**: in `expandMaintenancePolicy()`, when building the `MaintenanceWindow` for whichever type is configured, explicitly set `NullFields` for the sibling types being vacated, e.g. for `recurring_window`:

```go
window := &container.MaintenanceWindow{
    MaintenanceExclusions: exclusions,
    RecurringWindow: &container.RecurringTimeWindow{...},
}
window.NullFields = append(window.NullFields, "DailyMaintenanceWindow", "RecurringMaintenanceWindow")
```

(symmetrically for the other two branches).

**Workaround**: run `gcloud container clusters update <cluster> --maintenance-window-start=... --maintenance-window-end=... --maintenance-window-recurrence=...` (or the daily-window equivalent) once, outside Terraform. That client path clears the sibling field correctly, so the real resource matches and the next `plan` comes back clean.

### References

* `google-api-go-client`: `container/v1/container-gen.go`, `MaintenanceWindow` struct and its `MarshalJSON`/`NullFields` mechanism.

issue.title: google_container_cluster: switching maintenance_policy window type (daily ↔ recurring) never clears the previous window, causing a perpetual diff

labels.name: forward/review
labels.description: In review; remove label to forward

issue.body:
### Community Note

* Please vote on this issue by adding a 👍 [reaction](https://blog.github.com/2016-03-10-add-reactions-to-pull-requests-issues-and-comments/) to the original issue to help the community and maintainers prioritize this request.
* Please do not leave _+1_ or _me too_ comments, they generate extra noise for issue followers and do not help prioritize the request.
* If you are interested in working on this issue or have submitted a pull request, please leave a comment.
* If an issue is assigned to a user, that user is claiming responsibility for the issue.

### Terraform Version & Provider Version(s)

Reproduced against current `master` of `resource_container_cluster.go` (shared source between `google` and `google-beta` via magic-modules); not tied to a specific released version.

### Affected Resource(s)

* `google_container_cluster`

### Terraform Configuration

Before:
```tf
resource "google_container_cluster" "example" {
  # ... other config

  maintenance_policy {
    daily_maintenance_window {
      start_time = "06:00"
    }
  }
}
```

After:
```tf
resource "google_container_cluster" "example" {
  # ... other config

  maintenance_policy {
    recurring_window {
      start_time = "2026-09-03T06:00:00Z"
      end_time   = "2026-09-03T10:00:00Z"
      recurrence = "FREQ=DAILY"
    }
  }
}
```

### Debug Output

Not applicable — this isn't a crash or an error, it's a silent no-op. See "Actual Behavior" for the observable symptom (a diff that never resolves).

### Expected Behavior

After `terraform apply`, the cluster's maintenance policy is `recurring_window` only, `daily_maintenance_window` is cleared, and the next `plan` is clean.

### Actual Behavior

`apply` succeeds and the provider's own state shows `recurring_window`, but the live GCP resource never actually drops `daily_maintenance_window` — confirmed with `gcloud container clusters describe <cluster> --format="yaml(maintenancePolicy)"`, which keeps returning:

```yaml
maintenancePolicy:
  window:
    dailyMaintenanceWindow:
      duration: PT4H0M0S
      startTime: '06:00'
    # recurringWindow never actually appears here
```

Because the real resource never matches config, every subsequent `plan`/`apply` detects the identical diff again and reapplies — forever, with no error surfaced anywhere.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Create a `google_container_cluster` with `maintenance_policy.daily_maintenance_window` set.
2. `terraform apply`.
3. Change the config to `maintenance_policy.recurring_window` instead (remove the `daily_maintenance_window` block).
4. `terraform apply` again — it reports success.
5. Run `terraform plan` — it shows the same `recurring_window` diff again, unchanged.
6. Independently check `gcloud container clusters describe <cluster> --format="yaml(maintenancePolicy)"` — `dailyMaintenanceWindow` is still present, `recurringWindow` never appears.

### Important Factoids

Root cause, traced in provider source (not inferred from behavior alone):

1. `resourceContainerClusterUpdate` calls the dedicated `Projects.Locations.Clusters.SetMaintenancePolicy` RPC on `d.HasChange("maintenance_policy")` (`resource_container_cluster.go:4991-5010`) — a whole-object-replace call, not a masked patch, so the API should apply the `window` oneof correctly given a request that omits the old branch.

2. `expandMaintenancePolicy()` (`resource_container_cluster.go:6324-6437`), when `recurring_window` is configured, builds:
   ```go
   &container.MaintenancePolicy{
       Window: &container.MaintenanceWindow{
           MaintenanceExclusions: exclusions,
           RecurringWindow: &container.RecurringTimeWindow{...},
       },
       ...
   }
   ```
   `DailyMaintenanceWindow` is left at its Go zero value (`nil`). Nothing sets `NullFields`/`ForceSendFields` for the sibling window type being vacated — the same gap exists in the `daily_maintenance_window` and `recurring_maintenance_window` branches.

3. In the generated `google-api-go-client` struct (`container/v1/container-gen.go`, `MaintenanceWindow`):
   ```go
   DailyMaintenanceWindow *DailyMaintenanceWindow `json:"dailyMaintenanceWindow,omitempty"`
   ...
   ForceSendFields []string `json:"-"`
   NullFields      []string `json:"-"`
   ```
   A `nil` pointer tagged `omitempty` is dropped from the JSON body entirely unless named in `NullFields`. Since `expandMaintenancePolicy()` never populates it, the outbound request simply never mentions `dailyMaintenanceWindow` — it isn't cleared, it's just absent, and GKE leaves the existing value untouched.

**Suggested fix**: in `expandMaintenancePolicy()`, when building the `MaintenanceWindow` for whichever type is configured, explicitly set `NullFields` for the sibling types being vacated, e.g. for `recurring_window`:

```go
window := &container.MaintenanceWindow{
    MaintenanceExclusions: exclusions,
    RecurringWindow: &container.RecurringTimeWindow{...},
}
window.NullFields = append(window.NullFields, "DailyMaintenanceWindow", "RecurringMaintenanceWindow")
```

(symmetrically for the other two branches).

**Workaround**: run `gcloud container clusters update <cluster> --maintenance-window-start=... --maintenance-window-end=... --maintenance-window-recurrence=...` (or the daily-window equivalent) once, outside Terraform. That client path clears the sibling field correctly, so the real resource matches and the next `plan` comes back clean.

### References

* `google-api-go-client`: `container/v1/container-gen.go`, `MaintenanceWindow` struct and its `MarshalJSON`/`NullFields` mechanism.
